addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# vLLM Semantic Router Agent Entry

This file is the short entrypoint for coding agents. The detailed human-readable system of record lives in [tools/agent/docs/README.md](tools/agent/docs/README.md). The executable rule layer lives in [tools/agent/repo-manifest.yaml](tools/agent/repo-manifest.yaml), [tools/agent/task-matrix.yaml](tools/agent/task-matrix.yaml), [tools/agent/skill-registry.yaml](tools/agent/skill-registry.yaml), [tools/agent/structure-rules.yaml](tools/agent/structure-rules.yaml), [tools/agent/maintainer-policy.yaml](tools/agent/maintainer-policy.yaml), and [tools/make/agent.mk](tools/make/agent.mk).

vLLM Semantic Router is an Envoy ExtProc request router for LLM inference. It
resolves a request-facing entrypoint to an isolated recipe, evaluates that
recipe's signals and projections, applies its decision and algorithm, then
invokes the selected backend and recipe-scoped plugins.

## Read First

1. [tools/agent/docs/README.md](tools/agent/docs/README.md)
2. [tools/agent/docs/repo-map.md](tools/agent/docs/repo-map.md)
3. [tools/agent/docs/environments.md](tools/agent/docs/environments.md)
4. [tools/agent/docs/change-surfaces.md](tools/agent/docs/change-surfaces.md)
5. `make agent-report ENV=cpu|amd CHANGED_FILES="..."`

## Native Discovery vs Routed Context

- Root startup should always discover this [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) entrypoint and the thin repo-native bridge at [.agents/skills/harness/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/harness/SKILL.md).
- Full task routing, primary-skill resolution, local-rule surfacing, loop-mode guidance, and validation planning still come from `make agent-report ENV=cpu|amd CHANGED_FILES="..."`.
- `tools/agent/**` remains the canonical harness source; `.agents/skills/**` is only a discovery bridge.

If you need real AMD model deployment details instead of the minimal smoke path, also read [website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md](website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md) and [config/recipes/balance/config.yaml](config/recipes/balance/config.yaml).

## Repository Map

- `src/semantic-router/`: Go router, Envoy ExtProc server, routing runtime, and APIs
- `src/vllm-sr/`: Python CLI and local stack orchestration
- `config/`: canonical config, reusable fragments, runtime examples, and complete recipes
- `candle-binding/`, `ml-binding/`, `nlp-binding/`, `onnx-binding/`: inference bindings
- `dashboard/`: React frontend and Go management backend
- `deploy/`: artifacts that create or configure deployment targets
- `e2e/`: end-to-end framework and profiles
- `tools/`: build, development, release, security, smoke, and agent tooling
- `website/`: the only public documentation tree

The root contains only repository-wide contracts, community metadata, and
tool-mandated entrypoints. The executable allowlist is in
`tools/agent/structure-rules.yaml`; do not add root catch-all files.

## Supported Environments

- `cpu-local`: `make vllm-sr-dev`, then `vllm-sr serve --image-pull-policy never`
- `amd-local`: `make vllm-sr-dev VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=amd`, then `vllm-sr serve --image-pull-policy never --platform amd`

- Keep commits reviewable and logically coherent. Each commit must build and lint, describe why the change exists, and avoid unrelated drive-by cleanup.
- Keep PR blast radius aligned with the requested behavior; couple subsystems only when their contracts change together.
- Maintainer release, issue, PR, stale-work, and daily-board workflows live in [tools/agent/docs/maintainer-ops.md](tools/agent/docs/maintainer-ops.md) and write local state only under `.agent-harness/maintainer/` unless an explicit reviewed apply step mutates GitHub.
- Behavior-visible routing, startup, config, Docker, CLI, or API changes need E2E updates unless the change is a pure refactor.
- If the work needs multiple resumable loops across sessions or contributors, use the indexed current execution plans under [tools/agent/docs/plans/README.md](tools/agent/docs/plans/README.md) instead of ad hoc task notes. Historical plans are not kept in the current tree.
- If the desired architecture and the current implementation still diverge after your change, add or update the durable debt entry indexed from [tools/agent/docs/tech-debt/README.md](tools/agent/docs/tech-debt/README.md) instead of leaving the gap only in chat or PR text.

# Repo Map

## Repository Asset Boundaries

- `config/` owns canonical router configuration, reusable fragments, complete
  use-case recipes, and backend runtime examples.
- `deploy/` owns only artifacts that create or configure a deployment target:
  Helm, Kubernetes, KServe, OpenShift, the operator, and local proxy manifests.
- `website/` is the sole public documentation tree.
- `tools/` owns build automation, developer utilities, smoke tests, model
  helpers, auxiliary test services, and this internal agent harness.

The repository intentionally has no root `docs/` or `scripts/` catch-all.
Place new assets by ownership and lifecycle instead of by file extension.

## Root Contract

The root is reserved for repository-wide contracts, community health files,
the public installer, and configuration files whose tools require root
discovery. Tool-specific configuration belongs with the tool:

- GitHub ownership metadata lives in `.github/CODEOWNERS`.
- CRD reference generation config lives in `tools/crd/ref-docs.yaml`.
- Security scanner policy lives in `tools/security/ast-scan-allowlist.txt`.
- Local editor or assistant files such as `.cursorrules`, `.opencode.yaml`, and
  `CLAUDE.md` are ignored; `AGENTS.md` is the single agent entrypoint.

`tools/agent/structure-rules.yaml` owns the executable root-file allowlist, and
the changed-file structure gate rejects unowned additions.

## Core Subsystems

- `src/semantic-router/`
  - Go router, Envoy extproc server, config loading, Kubernetes controller, routing logic
- `src/semantic-router/pkg/milvus/`
  - Shared Milvus dial, collection ensure/load, and retry helpers for memory, cache, vectorstore, replay, and extproc memory wiring (see issue #1601)
- `src/vllm-sr/`
  - Python CLI, config generation, Docker orchestration, local bootstrap flow
- `src/fleet-sim/`
  - Fleet simulator package, HTTP service, data sets, examples, and service image used by the dashboard sidecar
- `candle-binding/`, `ml-binding/`, `nlp-binding/`
  - Rust-backed inference and ML bindings used by the router
- `dashboard/`
  - Dashboard frontend and backend
- `deploy/operator/`
  - Kubernetes operator, CRD schema, and controller-facing deployment contract
- `src/training/`
  - classifier/post-training scripts, training utilities, and evaluation-oriented model workflows
- `e2e/`
  - kind/Kubernetes E2E framework and profile matrix
- `tools/make/`
  - canonical automation entry points
- `tools/agent/`
  - coding-agent manifests, scripts, skills, and structure rules

## Known Hotspots

- `src/semantic-router/pkg/config/config.go`
  - central config type table; prefer moving plugin contracts and helper methods into adjacent files
- `src/semantic-router/pkg/config/validator.go`
  - semantic validation hotspot; keep family-specific checks and inventories in sibling validator files instead of widening one entrypoint
- `src/semantic-router/pkg/config/rag_plugin.go`
  - plugin-config hotspot; keep backend-specific RAG payloads, decode helpers, and validation branches in adjacent modules as the matrix grows

- `src/semantic-router/pkg/extproc/processor_res_body.go`
  - response-body orchestration hotspot; keep provider normalization, streaming, replay/cache, and response-warning helpers separate
- `src/fleet-sim/fleet_sim/optimizer/base.py`
  - fleet-sim optimizer hotspot; keep analytical sizing, DES verification, and report-oriented helpers on separate seams
- `deploy/operator/api/v1alpha1/semanticrouter_types.go`
  - operator schema hotspot; keep CRD contract families and comments readable instead of widening one type table
- `deploy/operator/controllers/canonical_config_builder.go`
  - operator canonical-config hotspot; keep family-specific translation and backend discovery out of one builder seam
- `dashboard/frontend/src/App.tsx`
  - dashboard route-shell hotspot; keep auth/setup gating and layout composition separate from page-specific logic
- `dashboard/frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx`
  - dashboard overview hotspot; keep fetch shaping, quick-action composition, and render fragments out of one page shell

  - acceptance coverage hotspot; keep contract assertions separate from report-only metrics and stress dashboards

- `dashboard/frontend/src/components/ExpressionBuilder.tsx`
  - expression editor hotspot; keep AST/tree helpers and reusable render fragments outside the main ReactFlow container
- `dashboard/backend/handlers/config.go`, `dashboard/backend/handlers/deploy.go`, `dashboard/backend/handlers/status.go`, `dashboard/backend/handlers/status_modes.go`
  - dashboard backend control hotspots; keep HTTP transport thin and move file mutation, runtime apply, container probing, and status synthesis into adjacent helpers

- Root command router: [Makefile](../../../Makefile)

59	func applyBackendRuntimeTuningDefaults() {
60		backend := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(os.Getenv("EMBEDDING_BACKEND_OVERRIDE")))
61		if backend != "candle" {
62			return
63		}
64	
65		defaults := map[string]string{
66			"OMP_NUM_THREADS":        "1",
67			"MKL_NUM_THREADS":        "1",
68			"OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS":   "1",
69			"RAYON_NUM_THREADS":      "1",
70			"TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM": "false",
71		}
72		applied := make(map[string]string)
73		for key, value := range defaults {
74			if _, exists := os.LookupEnv(key); exists {
75				continue
76			}
77			if err := os.Setenv(key, value); err != nil {
78				logging.ComponentWarnEvent("router", "backend_runtime_tuning_setenv_failed", map[string]interface{}{
79					"backend": backend,
80					"env":     key,
81					"error":   err.Error(),
82				})
83				continue
84			}
85			applied[key] = value
86		}
87		if len(applied) == 0 {
88			return
89		}
90		logging.ComponentEvent("router", "backend_runtime_tuning_applied", map[string]interface{}{
91			"backend": backend,
92			"env":     applied,
93		})
94	}
95	
96	func ensureModelsDownloaded(cfg *config.RouterConfig, startupWriter startupstatus.StatusWriter) error {
97		reporter := func(progress modeldownload.ProgressState) {
98			state := startupstatus.State{
99				Ready:            false,
100				DownloadingModel: progress.DownloadingModel,
101				PendingModels:    progress.PendingModels,
102				ReadyModels:      progress.ReadyModels,
103				TotalModels:      progress.TotalModels,
104				Message:          progress.Message,
105			}
106	
107			switch progress.Phase {
108			case "downloading":
109				state.Phase = "downloading_models"
110			case "completed":
111				state.Phase = "initializing_models"
112				state.Message = "Required router models downloaded. Continuing startup..."
113			case "skipped":
114				state.Phase = "initializing_models"
115			default:
116				state.Phase = "checking_models"
117			}
118	
119			if err := startupWriter.Write(state); err != nil {
120				logging.ComponentWarnEvent("router", "model_download_progress_persist_failed", map[string]interface{}{
121					"phase":             state.Phase,
122					"downloading_model": state.DownloadingModel,
123					"ready_models":      state.ReadyModels,
124					"total_models":      state.TotalModels,
125					"error":             err.Error(),
126				})
127			}
128		}
129	
130		return modeldownload.EnsureModelsForConfigWithProgress(cfg, reporter)
131	}
132	
133	func applyKubernetesConfigUpdate(newConfig *config.RouterConfig) error {
134		if err := ensureKubernetesConfigModels(newConfig); err != nil {
135			return fmt.Errorf("failed to ensure models for kubernetes config update: %w", err)
136		}
137	
138		replaceKubernetesRuntimeConfig(newConfig)
139		logging.ComponentEvent("router", "kubernetes_config_applied", map[string]interface{}{
140			"config_source":  newConfig.ConfigSource,
141			"decision_count": len(newConfig.Decisions),
142		})
143		return nil
144	}
145	
146	// startKubernetesController starts the Kubernetes controller for watching CRDs
147	func startKubernetesController(staticConfig *config.RouterConfig, kubeconfig, namespace string) {
148		// Import k8s package here to avoid import errors when k8s dependencies are not available
149		// This is a lazy import pattern
150		logging.ComponentEvent("router", "kubernetes_controller_starting", map[string]interface{}{
151			"namespace":      namespace,
152			"has_kubeconfig": kubeconfig != "",
153		})
154	
155		controller, err := k8s.NewController(k8s.ControllerConfig{
156			Namespace:      namespace,
157			Kubeconfig:     kubeconfig,
158			StaticConfig:   staticConfig,
159			OnConfigUpdate: applyKubernetesConfigUpdate,
160		})
161		if err != nil {
162			logging.ComponentFatalEvent("router", "kubernetes_controller_create_failed", map[string]interface{}{
163				"namespace": namespace,
164				"error":     err.Error(),
165			})
166		}
167	
168		ctx := context.Background()
169		if err := controller.Start(ctx); err != nil {
170			logging.ComponentFatalEvent("router", "kubernetes_controller_failed", map[string]interface{}{
171				"namespace": namespace,
172				"error":     err.Error(),
173			})
174		}
175	}
176	
177	// logStartupSummary emits a single structured log line summarizing the router
178	// startup state — making it trivial for agents and log aggregators to determine
179	// what the router is serving and on which ports.
180	func logStartupSummary(cfg *config.RouterConfig, opts runtimeOptions, embeddingModelsReady bool) {
181		decisionNames := make([]string, 0, len(cfg.Decisions))
182		for _, d := range cfg.Decisions {
183			decisionNames = append(decisionNames, d.Name)
184		}
185	
186		logging.ComponentEvent("router", "startup_complete", map[string]interface{}{
187			"extproc_port":        opts.port,
188			"api_port":            opts.apiPort,
189			"metrics_port":        opts.metricsPort,
190			"secure":              opts.secure,
191			"config_source":       cfg.ConfigSource,
192			"decisions":           strings.Join(decisionNames, ","),
193			"embedding_ready":     embeddingModelsReady,
194			"sem_cache_enabled":   cfg.Enabled,
195			"model_selection":     cfg.ModelSelection.Enabled,
196			"authz_providers":     len(cfg.Authz.Providers),
197			"ratelimit_providers": len(cfg.RateLimit.Providers),
198		})
199	}

# Maintained routing recipes

`config/recipes/` contains complete, executable use-case deliveries. Directory
names describe the user outcome; implementation names such as Router Flow,
SAARS, or MMLU belong inside the recipe documentation rather than in the
catalog taxonomy.

## Delivery contract

Every child directory has the same four files:

- `config.yaml` — canonical v0.3 runtime configuration.
- `recipe.dsl` — reviewable routing policy that compiles back into the same
  dynamic routing surface.
- `probes.yaml` — backend-independent `/api/v1/eval` correctness probes.
- `README.md` — intended use, routing policy, tradeoffs, and validation steps.

The repository contract tests reject incomplete directories, invalid YAML or
DSL, and YAML/DSL drift.

## Catalog

| Use case | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`accuracy`](accuracy/README.md) | Spend bounded multi-model orchestration only where it has an expected quality benefit; keep long context single-model. |
| [`agent`](agent/README.md) | Route agent, coding, specialist, privacy, and security work across local and frontier lanes. |
| [`balance`](balance/README.md) | General-purpose quality, latency, and cost balance for a single default routing profile. |
| [`feedback`](feedback/README.md) | Recover from corrections, repeated dissatisfaction, failed code, and verification requests. |
| [`knowledge`](knowledge/README.md) | Use KB evidence to decide whether a knowledge-domain question merits frontier escalation. |
| [`multi-objective`](multi-objective/README.md) | Expose isolated balanced, speed, cost, accuracy, and privacy recipes as request-facing entrypoints. |
| [`privacy`](privacy/README.md) | Keep sensitive, suspicious, and private-context traffic on policy-compatible models. |

`bounded-candidate-iteration.dsl` and other syntax-only demonstrations are not
deployable recipes. Their behavior is covered by DSL unit tests instead of
being mixed into this catalog.

## Validate a recipe

From the repository root:

```bash
vllm-sr validate --config config/recipes/<use-case>/config.yaml

(cd src/semantic-router && \
  go run ./cmd/dsl validate ../../config/recipes/<use-case>/recipe.dsl)

(cd src/semantic-router && \
  go run ./cmd/dsl compile \
    --base ../../config/recipes/<use-case>/config.yaml \
    -o /tmp/<use-case>.yaml \
    ../../config/recipes/<use-case>/recipe.dsl)
```

Run the backend-independent calibration suite against a live router:

```bash
python tools/agent/scripts/router_calibration_loop.py \
  eval \
  --router-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 \
  --probes config/recipes/<use-case>/probes.yaml
```

The multi-objective profile additionally checks requested model, selected
recipe, decision, algorithm, plugins, signal evidence, multilingual variants,
multi-turn/tool shapes, and long-context boundaries. Every maintained manifest
also declares bounded concurrency, so the same report records end-to-end p50,
p95, and p99 Eval latency, throughput, and transport errors alongside routing

---
sidebar_position: 1
description: Research-driven introduction to vLLM Semantic Router, an Envoy-based control plane for signal-aware LLM routing, policy enforcement, and token efficiency.
---

# vLLM Semantic Router

**We believe Mixture-of-Models is the next-generation model architecture for
heterogeneous LLM inference.**

**That is why we built vLLM Semantic Router**—to turn signals and preferences
into executable model paths for every user, product, and workload.

The project sits between clients and model backends as an Envoy External
Processor (`ext_proc`), turning routing from ad hoc application logic into an
observable, configurable control plane for multi-model systems.

## Research Focus

We use the project to answer a small set of hard systems questions:

1. **How do we capture missing signals** from requests, responses, users, and runtime context?
2. **How do we compose those signals** into robust routing and policy decisions?
3. **How do multiple models collaborate** as a system instead of serving as isolated endpoints?
4. **How do we optimize latency, spend, and tool usage** as part of a practical token economy?
5. **How do we add safety, feedback, and observability** without fragmenting the serving stack?

## Core System

### Signal and Projection Routing

Captures **16 maintained signal families** and coordinates them with reusable
projections before route selection:

| Layer           | Components                                                                                                                                                               | Role                                                      |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Signals**     | `authz`, `context`, `keyword`, `language`, `structure`, `complexity`, `domain`, `embedding`, `kb`, `modality`, `fact-check`, `jailbreak`, `pii`, `preference`, `reask`, `user-feedback` | Extract reusable request, safety, follow-up, and preference facts |
| **Projections** | `partitions`, `scores`, `mappings`                                                                                                                                       | Coordinate competing matches and emit named routing bands |
| **Decisions**   | AND/OR policy rules over signals and projections                                                                                                                         | Select the active route and model candidates              |

**How it works**: Signals are extracted from requests, projections coordinate
matched evidence, decision rules evaluate the resulting facts, and the chosen
route drives plugins plus model dispatch.

### Plugin Chain Architecture

Extensible plugin system for request/response processing:

| Plugin Type         | Description                                   | Use Case                                      |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| **semantic-cache**  | Semantic similarity-based caching             | Reduce latency and costs for similar queries  |
| **jailbreak**       | Adversarial prompt detection                  | Block prompt injection and jailbreak attempts |
| **pii**             | Personally identifiable information detection | Protect sensitive data and ensure compliance  |
| **system_prompt**   | Dynamic system prompt injection               | Add context-aware instructions per route      |
| **header_mutation** | HTTP header manipulation                      | Control routing and backend behavior          |
| **hallucination**   | Token-level hallucination detection           | Real-time fact verification during generation |

**How it works**: Plugins form a processing chain, each plugin can inspect/modify requests and responses, with configurable enable/disable per decision.

## Key Benefits

### A Control Plane for LLMRouting

- **Policy instead of hard-coded branches**: Move routing logic out of application code into reusable signals, decisions, and configuration.
- **Capability-aware selection**: Route by task shape, risk, and quality requirements instead of defaulting every request to one model.

### A Practical Token Economy Layer

- **Spend budget where it matters**: Reserve premium models, long context, and tool calls for the requests that need them.
- **Reduce waste without collapsing quality**: Use semantic caching, context-aware routing, and explicit policy to control latency and token spend.

### Governance in the Request Path

- **Built-in safety and compliance**: Apply jailbreak, PII, hallucination, prompt, and header controls at the same layer that makes routing decisions.
- **Observable decisions**: Keep routing and policy outcomes auditable so teams can tune behavior with data instead of guesswork.

### A Research Surface That Can Ship

- **Fast experimentation**: Add new signals, algorithms, and plugins without rewriting the serving path.
- **Production alignment**: Connect experimentation, observability, and deployment in one maintained system.

## Use Cases

- **Multi-model inference gateways**: Route to specialized models based on capability, context, and policy.
- **Cost-aware copilots**: Balance quality, latency, and spend for internal assistants and developer tooling.
- **Safety-sensitive assistants**: Enforce PII, jailbreak, and hallucination controls in the live request path.
- **Research platforms**: Evaluate routing policies, collect feedback signals, and iterate on model collaboration strategies.

## Start Here

- [**Overview**](overview/goals) for project goals, semantic routing concepts, and collective intelligence.
- [**Installation**](installation) for setup, deployment options, and configuration.
- [**Fleet Simulator**](fleet-sim/overview) for planning GPU fleets, evaluating routing strategies, and reading the guide PDF.
- [**Capacities**](tutorials/signal/overview) for signals, projections, decisions, plugins, algorithms, and global controls.
- [**Proposals**](proposals/unified-config-contract-v0-3) for design work that has not yet been folded into the stable docs set.

## Contributing

We welcome contributions! Please see our [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for details.

## License

This project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License - see the [LICENSE](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/blob/main/LICENSE) file for details.

"""vLLM Semantic Router CLI main entry point."""

from __future__ import annotations

import click

from cli import __version__
from cli.commands.chat import chat
from cli.commands.completion import completion
from cli.commands.eval import eval
from cli.commands.general import config, model, rag, validate
from cli.commands.runtime import dashboard, logs, serve, status, stop

logo = r"""
       _ _     __  __       ____  ____
__   _| | |_ _|  \/  |     / ___||  _ \
\ \ / / | | | | |\/| |_____\___ \| |_) |
 \ V /| | | |_| | |  |_____|___) |  _ <
  \_/ |_|_|\__,_|_|  |     |____/|_| \_\

vLLM Semantic Router - Intelligent routing for vLLM
"""

REGISTERED_COMMANDS = (
    serve,
    config,
    validate,
    model,
    rag,
    eval,
    status,
    logs,
    stop,
    dashboard,
    chat,
    completion,
)


@click.group(invoke_without_command=True)
@click.option("--version", is_flag=True, help="Show version and exit.")
@click.pass_context
def main(ctx: click.Context, version: bool) -> None:
    """vLLM Semantic Router CLI - Intelligent routing and caching for vLLM endpoints."""
    if version:
        click.echo(f"vllm-sr version: {__version__}")
        ctx.exit()

    if ctx.invoked_subcommand is None:
        click.echo(logo)
        click.echo(ctx.get_help())


for command in REGISTERED_COMMANDS:
    main.add_command(command)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## How DSL/Expressions Make Routing Decisions

1. **Parse** (`dsl/parser.go`): DSL source → raw AST (`rawProgram`) → resolved AST (`Program` with `RouteDecl`, `SignalDecl`, `BoolExpr` nodes)

3. **Evaluate** (`pkg/decision/engine.go`):

   - Leaf nodes call `matchesSignalType()` which checks if the signal name exists in `SignalMatches` (e.g., `KeywordRules`, `DomainRules`, `JailbreakRules`)

4. **Select** (`pkg/decision/engine.go`):

## How DSL/Expressions Make Routing Decisions

**DSL Flow:**

1. **Parse** (`dsl/parser.go`): DSL source → raw AST (`rawProgram`) → resolved AST (`Program` with `RouteDecl`, `SignalDecl`, `BoolExpr` nodes)

2. **Compile** (`dsl/compiler.go`):
   - `Compile()` calls `Parse()` then `CompileAST()`
   - `compileRoutes()` transforms each `RouteDecl` → `config.Decision`
   - `compileRouteRules()` converts `When` (BoolExpr tree) → `config.RuleCombination` with AND/OR/NOT operators
   - `compileSignalRefExpr()` maps leaf `SignalRefExpr` → `config.RuleNode` with Type/Name/Label/Predicate fields

3. **Evaluate** (`pkg/decision/engine.go`):
   - `DecisionEngine.evalNode()` recursively walks the `RuleCombination` tree
   - Leaf nodes call `matchesSignalType()` which checks if the signal name exists in `SignalMatches` (e.g., `KeywordRules`, `DomainRules`, `JailbreakRules`)
   - Composite nodes apply boolean logic: `evalAND()` (all children match, avg confidence), `evalOR()` (best-confidence match), `evalNOT()` (negation)
   - `evaluatePredicateLeaf()` handles numeric thresholds (`GT`, `GTE`, `LT`, `LTE`) on `SignalValues` or `SignalConfidences`

4. **Select** (`pkg/decision/engine.go`):
   - `selectBestDecision()` orders by strategy: tier-based (Tier < Confidence < Priority), confidence-based (Confidence > Priority), or priority-based (Priority > Confidence)

input.rationale: 本项目是面向 LLM 推理的 Envoy ExtProc 控制面（Go 路由器为核心，辅以 Python CLI、推理绑定、K8s Operator、React 面板、E2E 与仿真），体量大、跨语言，因此采用「先全局后内核、先概念后源码」的三层路径。入门层（U1–U3）先让读者建立 Mixture-of-Models + 信号-投影-决策的心智模型，再掌握 vllm-sr CLI 的运行方式与 v0.3 配置/Recipe 体系，建立可直接跑起来的能力。进阶层（U4–U9）沿着真实请求主链路 Envoy→ExtProc→分类信号→投影→决策→选择→后端 展开，并深入向量检索、语义缓存与记忆等运行时子系统，同时讲解可把 YAML 与 DSL 互转的路由 DSL。专家层（U10–U14）覆盖插件链、控制面 API、可观测性、多后端适配、Operator/CRD 与推理绑定、面板、E2E 与仿真、训练评估等扩展与工程化主题。单元之间遵循「概念→配置→启动→请求链路→决策选择→DSL→信号→存储缓存→插件→控制面→部署→面板→测试」的依赖顺序，每篇讲义只解决一个独立主题、引用 1–6 个真实源码文件并给出可操作的实践任务。

lectures.title: 嵌入提供者（Embedding Provider）

data.head: 7a77e1e1b1d5711d0b94e3c75bcea694a1d1f246
data.rationale: 本项目是面向 LLM 推理的 Envoy ExtProc 控制面（Go 路由器为核心，辅以 Python CLI、推理绑定、K8s Operator、React 面板、E2E 与仿真），体量大、跨语言，因此采用「先全局后内核、先概念后源码」的三层路径。入门层（U1–U3）先让读者建立 Mixture-of-Models + 信号-投影-决策的心智模型，再掌握 vllm-sr CLI 的运行方式与 v0.3 配置/Recipe 体系，建立可直接跑起来的能力。进阶层（U4–U9）沿着真实请求主链路 Envoy→ExtProc→分类信号→投影→决策→选择→后端 展开，并深入向量检索、语义缓存与记忆等运行时子系统，同时讲解可把 YAML 与 DSL 互转的路由 DSL。专家层（U10–U14）覆盖插件链、控制面 API、可观测性、多后端适配、Operator/CRD 与推理绑定、面板、E2E 与仿真、训练评估等扩展与工程化主题。单元之间遵循「概念→配置→启动→请求链路→决策选择→DSL→信号→存储缓存→插件→控制面→部署→面板→测试」的依赖顺序，每篇讲义只解决一个独立主题、引用 1–6 个真实源码文件并给出可操作的实践任务。

learning_goals: 理解项目要解决的问题：质量、成本、延迟、隐私、安全的可编程路由

units.title: 核心概念模型：信号-投影-决策

lectures.title: Projections：分区/评分/映射

learning_goals: 理解 partition 的 softmax_exclusive 语义与 default 兜底
理解 score 的 weighted_sum 加权组合方法
理解 mapping 的 threshold_bands 与 sigmoid_distance 校准
lectures.practice_task: 解析 balance 的 difficulty_score 评分投影，列出它用到的全部输入及其权重正负含义；再解释 difficulty_band 把分数切成哪几段命名带。

lectures.title: Decisions/Routes/Models：决策路由与模型
lectures.topic: 讲解 ROUTE 上的 WHEN 布尔规则、PRIORITY/TIER 优先级、MODEL 选择与 reasoning/effort 参数，以及决策如何映射到模型候选。
learning_goals: 理解 ROUTE 的 WHEN 规则在信号/投影上的 AND/OR/NOT 组合
理解 PRIORITY 与 TIER 如何决定路由命中顺序与兜底
理解 MODEL 声明与 capabilities/quality_score/tags 的作用
lectures.practice_task: 为 balance 中的 fast_qa 与 casual_chat 两条路由写一段：它们各自的 WHEN 条件、优先级差异，以及为什么 casual_chat 作为最终兜底没有 WHEN。

lectures.title: config.yaml v0.3 整体结构
lectures.topic: 讲解 v0.3 运行时配置的顶层结构：version、listeners、providers、routing、entrypoints、recipes、global 各段职责。
learning_goals: 掌握 config.yaml 的七大顶层段落及其作用
理解 entrypoints 与 recipes 的请求面到配方的映射关系
了解 global 段承载的全局控制项
lectures.practice_task: 在 config/config.yaml 中定位七大顶层段，统计 routing 段下 decisions、signals、projections、plugins 各有多少条目，并解释 entrypoints 如何把请求指到 recipe。

lectures.title: Recipes：可用的路由配方
lectures.topic: 讲解 config/recipes 下 balance/accuracy/agent/privacy/knowledge/feedback/multi-objective 等配方的用途与四件套交付契约（config.yaml/recipe.dsl/probes.yaml/README.md）。
learning_goals: 理解每个 recipe 解决的一个用户结果场景
掌握 recipe 的四文件交付契约与契约校验
了解 multi-objective 多入口配方的设计
lectures.practice_task: 对比 balance 与 privacy 两个配方的 README，总结它们的路由策略差异；运行 `vllm-sr validate --config config/recipes/balance/config.yaml` 并记录校验结果。

lectures.title: 配置加载与校验
lectures.topic: 讲解 Go 端配置加载（Parse/Load/Replace）、规范化与语义校验机制，以及全局热替换的入口。
learning_goals: 理解 config.Parse/Load 如何把 YAML 解析为 RouterConfig
理解 validator 的语义校验职责与家族化拆分约定
了解 config.Replace 在热重载/K8s 配置更新中的作用
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 loader.go 与 config.go，梳理 RouterConfig 的核心字段；找一个 validator 的校验规则，描述它阻止了哪类错误配置。

units.title: 路由器启动与 ExtProc 服务

lectures.title: 启动主流程：main.go 启动序列
lectures.topic: 逐段讲解 cmd/main.go 的启动序列：解析选项、加载配置、建 Registry、起 API Server、下载模型、初始化依赖、起 ExtProc、热身、标记就绪。
learning_goals: 掌握 main() 中各初始化步骤的顺序与依赖关系
理解 API Server 提前启动以暴露 /startup-status 的设计
了解模型下载进度上报与 startup 状态机
lectures.practice_task: 把 main() 的启动步骤画成时序图，并标注哪一步会让 /startup-status 可用、哪一步会因模型下载失败而 fatal。

lectures.title: Runtime Registry：运行时依赖容器
lectures.topic: 讲解 routerruntime.Registry 作为 ExtProc 与 API Server 之间共享的线程安全依赖容器，托管分类服务、记忆、向量库、模型选择与学习运行时。
learning_goals: 理解 Registry 承载的运行时依赖种类
理解 ExtProc 与 API Server 共享运行时依赖的方式
了解学习运行时（LearningRuntime）等窄接口缝
lectures.practice_task: 列出 Registry 暴露的 Set*/Get* 方法，说明 ExtProc 与 API Server 分别会注入/读取哪些依赖。

lectures.title: ExtProc gRPC 服务与 Router
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/extproc 的 Server 生命周期与 OpenAIRouter 核心状态机，以及 Envoy ExtProc 的 headers/body 交互模型。
learning_goals: 理解 ExtProc Server 的 NewServer/Start/GetRouter 生命周期
理解 OpenAIRouter 作为请求处理状态机的角色
了解 Envoy 通过 ExtProc gRPC 传递 headers→body→response 的交互
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 server.go 与 router.go，说明 Process(stream) 是如何被 Envoy 调用的，并描述 OpenAIRouter 持有哪些核心状态字段。

lectures.title: 请求体处理与入口解析
lectures.topic: 讲解 handleRequestBody 解析 OpenAI 请求体、resolveEntrypointForRequest 解析配方/入口，并进入决策求值前的准备。
learning_goals: 理解请求体如何被解析出 model/content
理解 entrypoint/recipe 解析与 passthrough 的区别
了解决策求值前的信号输入构建
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪一次 /v1/chat/completions 请求，描述它在 processor_req_body.go 中从解析 body 到确定 recipe 的调用顺序。

lectures.title: 决策求值管线：信号→决策
lectures.topic: 讲解 performDecisionEvaluation 如何准备信号、求值信号、调用决策引擎并选出匹配路由，是请求链路的内核。
learning_goals: 理解 prepareSignalEvaluationInput 与 evaluateSignalsForDecision 的衔接
理解 runDecisionEngine 调用决策引擎得到 DecisionResult
理解决策方法到选择算法的解析
lectures.practice_task: 在 req_filter_classification.go 中找到 performDecisionEvaluation 的主体，列出它调用的关键子步骤；并用 decision/engine.go 解释 EvaluateDecisionsWithSignals 的输入输出。

lectures.title: 响应体处理与插件回调
lectures.topic: 讲解 handleResponseBody 的响应体编排：provider 归一化、流式处理、缓存/重放写入与响应告警。
learning_goals: 理解响应体处理如何归一化不同 provider 的响应
理解流式响应的处理方式
了解响应阶段如何回写缓存与重放记录
lectures.practice_task: 梳理 processor_res_body.go 中响应处理的主要分支，说明流式与非流式响应分别走哪条路径，以及缓存命中的请求在响应阶段如何处理。

lectures.title: 决策引擎：布尔规则求值与置信度
lectures.topic: 深入 decision/engine.go：递归求值 RuleCombination 规则树、按信号类型匹配、AND/OR/NOT 布尔语义与置信度聚合，以及按 tier/confidence/priority 选择最佳决策。
learning_goals: 理解 evalNode 递归求值规则树的过程
理解 matchesSignalType 的存在性匹配与 domain 别名匹配
理解 AND 平均置信度、OR 取最佳置信度的聚合规则
lectures.practice_task: 构造一条含 AND/OR/NOT 的决策规则，手工推演它在给定信号匹配下的求值结果与聚合置信度；解释三种选择策略的差异。

lectures.title: 选择算法注册表：Elo/Hybrid 等
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/selection 的 Selector 接口、Registry 与多种算法实现（Elo、Hybrid、AutoMix、Session-aware、Static 等）及工厂。
learning_goals: 理解 Selector 接口与 SelectionContext/SelectionResult
理解 Registry 注册多种选择方法的方式
了解 Elo（Bradley-Terry）与 Hybrid 组合算法的思路
lectures.practice_task: 列出 factory.go 注册的所有选择方法；选择 Elo 算法，解释它如何用 Bradley-Terry 模型给候选模型打分并选出胜者。

lectures.title: 模型运行时、库存与定价
lectures.topic: 讲解 modelruntime 的嵌入模型初始化与热身、modelinventory 的外部模型目录类型、modelpricing 的成本计算。
learning_goals: 理解 PrepareRouterRuntime/WarmupRouter 如何初始化嵌入并加载工具/知识库
理解外部模型库存（ExternalModelConfig）的用途
了解 modelpricing 如何支撑成本感知路由
lectures.practice_task: 描述 PrepareRouterRuntime 返回的 EmbeddingRuntimeState 中 AnyReady/ToolsReady 的含义；并说明 modelpricing 在一次选择中可能如何影响候选排序。

lectures.title: DSL 语法与 AST
lectures.topic: 讲解路由 DSL 的 SIGNAL/PROJECTION/MODEL/PLUGIN/ROUTE/RECIPE/ENTRYPOINT/TEST 块语法，以及 parser.go 到 ast.go 的 AST 结构。
learning_goals: 掌握 DSL 各类块的定义语法
理解 Program/RouteDecl/SignalDecl/BoolExpr 等 AST 节点
理解 WHEN 布尔表达式（BoolAnd/BoolOr/BoolNot/SignalRefExpr）
lectures.practice_task: 用 DSL 语法手写一个包含 1 个 SIGNAL、1 个 PROJECTION 和 1 个 ROUTE（含 AND/NOT）的最小策略，并对照 ast.go 说明它会解析成哪些节点。

lectures.title: DSL 编译与反编译（YAML 往返）
lectures.topic: 讲解 compiler.go 把 AST 编译为 RouterConfig、compiler_routes/signals 的逐块编译，以及 decompiler/emitter_yaml 把配置反编译回 DSL/YAML 的往返能力。
learning_goals: 理解 Compile/CompileAST 把 AST 变成 RouterConfig 的流程
理解 ROUTE→Decision、SIGNAL→规则 的编译映射
理解 decompiler/emitter_yaml 实现的 YAML↔DSL 往返
minimal_modules: 反编译与 YAML 往返
lectures.practice_task: 把 balance 的 recipe.dsl 编译为 config.yaml，再把生成的 config.yaml 反编译回 DSL，对比两者是否一致并解释任何差异来源。

lectures.title: dsl 命令行工具
lectures.topic: 讲解 cmd/dsl 提供的 validate/compile/generate/test 子命令，作为编写与校验 recipe DSL 的开发者入口。
learning_goals: 掌握 dsl validate/compile 的命令用法
理解 test_runner 如何运行 DSL 内嵌的 TEST 块
了解 generate 的代码生成用途
lectures.practice_task: 对 config/recipes/<use-case>/recipe.dsl 运行 `go run ./cmd/dsl validate` 与 `compile`，记录输出；再为一个 ROUTE 编写一个 TEST 块并运行 test_runner。

lectures.title: 分类编排与信号求值
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/classification 的 Classifier 编排所有分类后端、EvaluateAllSignals 抽取全部信号，以及把信号桥接到决策引擎的过程。
learning_goals: 理解 Classifier 编排的各类分类后端
理解 EvaluateAllSignals 产出 SignalResults 的结构
理解 classifier_signal_decision 如何桥接到决策引擎
lectures.practice_task: 梳理 EvaluateAllSignals 会触发哪些分类器，并说明 SignalResults 中的 MatchedKeywordRules/MatchedDomainRules/SignalConfidences 是如何被决策引擎消费的。

lectures.title: 域/类别分类器
lectures.topic: 讲解 domain/category 分类如何用嵌入与熵分析做多类别匹配，以及 KB 增强的类别分类。
learning_goals: 理解 category_classifier 的熵感知多类别输出
理解 domain 与 category 的别名/MMLU 映射
了解 KB 增强类别分类（category_kb）
lectures.practice_task: 用一段示例文本解释 category_classifier 如何输出多类别概率；说明为什么 domain('health') 在决策里能匹配到 health 类别。

lectures.title: PII 与越狱检测
lectures.topic: 讲解 PII token 分类与 allow-list、以及 BERT+对比学习的越狱检测，它们构成请求路径上的安全治理信号。
learning_goals: 理解 PII 检测的 token 分类与 allow-list 强制
理解越狱检测的 BERT+对比学习方法
了解两类信号如何驱动安全路由
lectures.practice_task: 构造一条含 PII 与一条疑似越狱的输入，描述两类分类器分别输出什么信号，并指出在 privacy recipe 中这些信号如何改变路由结果。

lectures.title: 嵌入提供者（Embedding Provider）
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/embedding 的 Provider 接口与工厂，作为分类、缓存、记忆、工具检索共用的嵌入能力抽象。
learning_goals: 理解 Provider 接口的 Embed/EmbedBatch/Dimension/Backend
理解从 RouterConfig 构造 Provider 的方式
了解嵌入在多子系统中的复用
lectures.practice_task: 说明 NewProviderFromRouterConfig 如何根据配置选择本地或远程嵌入后端；列出至少 3 个消费 Provider 的子系统。

units.title: 向量检索、语义缓存与记忆

lectures.title: HNSW 向量索引
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/hnsw 的纯 Go HNSW 近邻检索实现，包括图参数、增删查与 SIMD 距离优化。
learning_goals: 理解 HNSW 的 M/efConstruction/efSearch 参数
理解 Add/Search 的图检索流程
了解 SIMD（AVX2/AVX-512）点积优化
lectures.practice_task: 用 hnsw.NewIndex 构建一个小索引，插入若干向量并执行 Search，对比不同 efSearch 下的召回率与耗时。

lectures.title: 向量存储与多后端
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/vectorstore 的 OpenAI 兼容向量库 API、文档摄入流水线（切块→嵌入→写入）与多后端（内存/Milvus/Qdrant/Valkey/LlamaStack），以及 pkg/milvus 的连接与集合生命周期。
learning_goals: 理解 VectorStoreBackend 接口与切块/嵌入/写入流水线
理解多后端可替换的存储抽象
了解 milvus 的连接、集合 ensure/load 与重试
lectures.practice_task: 描述一次文档摄入从上传到可检索的完整流水线；并说明在内存与 Milvus 两种后端下，VectorStoreBackend 的实现差异。

lectures.title: 语义缓存
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/cache 的语义缓存：按查询嵌入相似度缓存请求-响应对、多后端（内存 HNSW/Milvus/Qdrant/Redis/Valkey/Hybrid）、用户作用域隔离与 OpenAI 查询抽取。
learning_goals: 理解 CacheBackend 接口与相似度查找
理解 hybrid 两级缓存（HNSW+Milvus）
理解用户作用域隔离（HMAC 命名空间）
lectures.practice_task: 解释 ScopeQueryToUser 如何用 HMAC 实现多租户隔离；并对比 inmemory 与 hybrid 两种缓存的查找路径。

lectures.title: 智能体记忆（Agentic Memory）
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/memory 的记忆系统：语义/程序/情景记忆类型、嵌入检索、自适应阈值、混合 BM25 重排与多后端存储。
learning_goals: 理解 Store 接口与 Memory/MemoryType 类型
理解记忆的嵌入检索与混合重排
了解记忆过滤器（MemoryFilter）的后处理
lectures.practice_task: 说明语义/程序/情景三种记忆的区别；描述一次 Retrieve 如何结合嵌入相似度与 BM25 重排选出最终记忆。

lectures.title: 插件链架构与配置
lectures.topic: 讲解插件链（semantic-cache/jailbreak/pii/system_prompt/header_mutation/hallucination/router_replay/rag 等）的配置片段、按 decision 启停与在请求/响应阶段的执行。
learning_goals: 理解插件类型目录与 config/plugin 下的配置片段
理解插件按 decision 启停与链式处理
了解 rag_plugin 等插件配置热点
lectures.practice_task: 在 config/plugin 下选择两个插件，说明它们的配置字段；并解释 router_replay 如何在请求与响应阶段捕获 body。

lectures.title: Prompt 压缩
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/promptcompression 的无 LLM 压缩：TextRank、位置加权（Lost in the Middle）、TF-IDF、新颖度四信号打分选句。
learning_goals: 理解四信号打分的句子选择机制
理解 TextRank 在句子邻接矩阵上的 PageRank
理解位置加权为何呈 U 形
lectures.practice_task: 用 DefaultConfig 对一段长文本运行 Compress，对比压缩前后 token 数；调整四类权重观察选句变化。

lectures.title: 工具检索与 MCP
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/tools 的语义工具库（嵌入检索 top-k 工具）与 pkg/mcp 的 Model Context Protocol 客户端（stdio/HTTP 传输、工具过滤）。
learning_goals: 理解 ToolsDatabase 的嵌入检索与点积打分
理解 MCPClient 接口与 stdio/HTTP 传输
了解工具过滤（allow/block）
lectures.practice_task: 描述 FindSimilarToolsWithScores 如何按查询嵌入检索工具；并说明一个 stdio 类型 MCP 服务如何被 factory 创建并连接。

lectures.title: 多后端适配（OpenAI/Anthropic/Response API/ImageGen）
lectures.topic: 讲解 OpenAI↔Anthropic 格式互转、Response API 状态化翻译、OpenAI 文件/向量库客户端与图像生成后端工厂。
learning_goals: 理解 Anthropic 请求/响应互转与 passthrough 字段
理解 Response API 的 previous_response_id 链式翻译
理解 imagegen 的后端工厂与请求参数
lectures.practice_task: 用一个 OpenAI chat 请求体说明 ToAnthropicRequestBody 做了哪些字段转换；并描述 Response API 如何把 previous_response_id 还原成完整上下文。

lectures.title: API Server 管理 API
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/apiserver 提供的管理面 HTTP API：配置部署/ETag、分类与评估路由、知识库与嵌入、鉴权与 OpenAPI 规范。
learning_goals: 理解管理 API 的路由组织与中间件
理解配置部署与运行时同步（ETag）
了解 classify/eval/kbs/embeddings 等能力端点
lectures.practice_task: 梳理 apiserver 暴露的主要路由前缀，并说明配置部署如何通过 ETag 实现运行时同步；用 OpenAPI spec 找到 classify 端点的入参。

lectures.title: 投影追踪与可解释性
lectures.topic: 讲解 projectiontrace 的版本化 JSON：分区解析（softmax 胜者与边际）、评分分解（加权贡献）、映射决策（阈值带与边界距离），供分类/重放/面板消费。
learning_goals: 理解 Trace 的 schema 版本与三大组成
理解 PartitionResolution/ScoreBreakdown/MappingDecision 字段
了解投影追踪在可解释性与面板中的复用
lectures.practice_task: 构造一个投影追踪 JSON 示例，解释 difficulty_score 的 ScoreBreakdown 中各输入的贡献，以及 difficulty_band 的 MappingDecision 选择了哪段带。

lectures.title: 限流、在途、延迟与授权
lectures.topic: 讲解请求路径上的治理控制：ratelimit 多 provider 链式（Envoy RLS/本地，RPM+TPM）、inflight 在途计数自愈、latency 缓存热度估计、authz 授权分类。
learning_goals: 理解 ratelimit 的 Provider 链与首拒语义
理解 inflight 的自愈老化与负载感知
理解 latency 的 TTFT 缓存热度估计与 authz 授权
lectures.practice_task: 说明 ratelimit 链式多 provider 的首拒语义；并解释 inflight 在漏掉 End 调用时如何自愈、latency 如何用 TTFT 估计缓存命中概率。

lectures.title: 可观测性：日志、指标、追踪
lectures.topic: 讲解 pkg/observability 的三大子能力（结构化日志、Prometheus 指标、OpenTelemetry 追踪）及其在 main 启动序列中的接入。
learning_goals: 理解结构化日志事件（ComponentEvent）的组织
理解 Prometheus 指标与 windowed metrics
理解 OpenTelemetry tracing 的初始化与采样
lectures.practice_task: 在 main.go 中定位 initializeTracing 与 startMetricsServerIfEnabled，说明指标端口与追踪初始化的时机；并解读 startup_complete 日志事件包含哪些字段。

lectures.title: vllm-sr 容器与运行时编排
lectures.topic: 讲解 Python CLI 如何编排本地容器栈：容器镜像/服务管理、运行时拓扑、生命周期与 K8s 后端抽象。
learning_goals: 理解 container_cli 的镜像/服务 barrel 设计
理解 runtime_stack/runtime_topology 的栈编排
了解 k8s_backend 与 deployment_backend 的后端抽象
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪 `vllm-sr serve` 在 core.py/runtime_stack.py 中的调用链，说明它如何拉起 Envoy、router、模型后端等服务并管理其生命周期。

lectures.title: Helm / Kubernetes / 本地部署
lectures.topic: 讲解 deploy/ 下创建与配置部署目标的产物：Helm chart、Kubernetes 清单、KServe、OpenShift 与本地代理清单。
learning_goals: 理解 deploy 的资产边界（只做创建/配置部署目标）
理解 Helm chart 与 Kubernetes 清单的组织
了解 local/openshift/kserve 等部署变体
lectures.practice_task: 在 deploy/helm 中找到 router 的 Deployment/Service 模板，说明 Envoy 与 ExtProc router 是如何被编排在一起的；记录关键可配置项。

lectures.title: Operator 与 CRD
